addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". docs(roadmap): F9 measured - 1.26x decode, 1.14-1.17x prefill
  node                        F8          F9    F9/F8   vs pristine
  K=51 decode  nrows=2    457,092     362,799    1.26x    12.34x
  K=51 prefill nrows=4    931,754     818,314    1.14x    10.85x
  K=56 prefill nrows=4  6,636,852   5,683,029    1.17x        -

The finding worth keeping is that decode and prefill are now bound by
different things. Cycles per issued instruction: the gemv is unchanged at
2.23 -> 2.24, so it is purely issue bound and F9 converted the instruction
saving 1:1 into cycles. The gemm's went 2.53 -> 4.84, so it is not issue
bound any more and cutting instructions further will not help prefill.
Corollary: F8's "instruction-issue floor" of 328,865 was never a floor, it
was an instruction count - F9 beat it at 362,799 with no HVM.

Also records the two things that did NOT work, so nobody repeats them:
grouping the widths in source (the scheduler undoes it, 4.00 -> only 2.00),
and 4 scratch registers instead of 2 (no spills, but 855,476 vs 818,314,
4.5% worse - so producer-consumer distance is not the gemm's limiter).
The experiment that would identify it, d4-nopf and d4-hvm on the prefill
node, is written down but not yet run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
perf(riscv): F9, one vsetvli per four dots instead of four per dot
The Q1_D4 kernels alternate between the byte view (mask load, sign expand)
and the 32-bit view (activation broadcast, the dot). Every alternation costs
a vsetvli that does no arithmetic: 4 per dot in the gemv, 40% of its inner
loop. GCC's share of that is that it cannot see inside an inline asm block,
so it assumes each one left vtype unknown and re-issues its own.

Grouping the two widths in the source is NOT enough - the scheduler
interleaves them again. Measured: source grouping alone only got the gemv
from 4.00 to 2.00 vsetvli per dot. So everything at e32 now lives inside one
asm block, the broadcasts included, leaving GCC only e8 work to schedule.

  vsetvli per dot (between first and last dot, O3): gemv 4.00 -> 0.94
                                                    gemm 2.00 -> 0.52
  instrs per dot:                                   gemv 10.00 -> 7.90
                                                    gemm  9.00 -> 4.13
The gemm gains more because the smaller body also let GCC unroll its column
loop 8x, which it would not do before. No vector spills.

Taking the activation quads as uint32 GPRs and spelling out vmv.v.x also
kills the vlse32 stride-0 trap by construction, so q1_bcast_act4 and its
barrier are gone.

Bit-identical, not just close: test-repack-q1_0 13/13 with every nmse
unchanged from the pre-F9 run (0.000e+00 on the gemv cases, 4.171e-15 /
1.282e-14 / 7.417e-15 on the gemm ones). Q1_D4=0 control also 13/13.
check-vd4dots.sh gains a VTYPE-CHURN budget of 1 vsetvli per dot, which
fails on the old code at O3 and passes now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
docs(roadmap): correct the F9 cause - e8/e32 ping-pong, not the asm
The entry blamed GCC re-emitting vsetvli after the inline asm. That is real
but it is only 1 of the 4 vsetvli per dot. The dominant cause is that the
work alternates between the byte view (vlm, vmerge) and the 32-bit view
(vmv.v.x, dot), and every alternation costs one - it would happen with no
inline asm at all. Widening the asm block therefore recovers 1 of 4, not
4 of 4; the fix is to batch by element width. Includes the real O3 listing
and marks the 1.5x as an instruction count, not measured cycles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
---

- The config tool AUTO-WIDENS 6 dependent widths (all +7): STLB_RAM_DW 60->67,

  CM_SNP_RAM_DW 21->28, L3C_TAG_RAM_DW 18->25. So NEVER hand-patch config.inc
  or a single cfg line - narrow TLB/cache tags would silently truncate
  addresses. Always regenerate (the standalone step is
  `NDS_HOME=<tree> tclsh <tree>/config_tools/nds-softcore-config --load <cfg> --generate`).
- **TIMING NEUTRAL, PROVEN**: same bin-prefetch, 4B K=51 node, BIU=39 engine
  1,384,130 cycles vs BIU=32 backup engine 1,384,130 - bit-identical, not
  "close". Expected: tag-RAM WIDTH does not change cache sets/ways or TLB entry
  count. Controlled A/B done by staging the backup in its own dir and pointing
  `VSIM_BIN_DIR` at it (driver/engine_registry.cpp:186 honours that env).

  needs vlinux to place its arenas at a non-zero ram_base = roadmap U10d, so
  U10f's "does the RTL address it" gate is BLOCKED ON U10d, not only on the
  engine rebuild.

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-1002/bundled-skills/2.1.220/dab44e2b452bab297a699615dd246640/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

Running Bonsai-8B, and what it buys

How the 4B flow was extended to the 8B model (two flags, zero rebuilds), and the measured speedup of the Q1_0 optimization chain on the same RTL node.

11.23xend-to-end speedup, pristine → vd4dots
7,278,168 → 648,246cycles, K=51 node (layer 7 V projection)
2 flags · 0 rebuildsall it takes to move from 4B to 8B

part 1

What must change to run the 8B model

The 4B recipe carries over unchanged: same four binaries, same engine, same ROI marker at K=51. The model file is a runtime argument. Only two flags are new, and both exist because the 8B model presses against the 2 GiB guest RAM window.

--mem-size 2097148K
andesim flag. The exact hybrid maximum: 2 GiB minus the 4 KiB hybrid scratch area. Hybrid mode rejects 2G outright (only fast mode accepts it), so this literal value is required.
--no-mmap
llama.cpp flag. On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack buffer type accepts these tensors, so with mmap the 1,099 MiB file mapping and the 931 MiB repack buffer are both resident at load time. Together with the other buffers that exceeds the window. --no-mmap drops the mapping; everything else fits with 565 MiB to spare.

The full command (the two 8B flags highlighted):

cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
Why the binaries need no rebuild

The ROI marker counts MUL_MAT nodes, not shapes. Bonsai-8B is the same qwen3 architecture as 4B — 36 layers, 253 MUL_MAT per token — so compiled-in K=51 lands on the same node: the layer-7 V projection. Only its shape grows, 2560×1024 → 4096×1024. Each run self-reports the node, so this is checked, not assumed:

[roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [4096 x 1024] nrows=2

The repack gate also passes untouched: 1024 output rows, and 1024 mod 64 = 0.

part 2

Speedup on the 8B node

Same optimization chain as 4B, measured on the K=51 node (blk.7.attn_v.weight 4096×1024, nrows=2, RTL cycles on ax46mpv_fpga_l3). Every stage keeps output bit-exact.

buildcyclessteptotal speedup4B total (ref)
pristine7,278,168—1.00x1.00x
repack3,475,1472.09x2.09x2.09x
+ prefetch2,218,5401.57x3.28x3.23x
+ vd4dots (F9)648,2463.42x11.23x12.34x

The chain transfers to 8B almost exactly. Repack and prefetch cost the same cycles per element as on 4B — the prefetch stage lands at 0.264 cyc/elem/act, inside the 0.261–0.265 band measured across all five 4B shapes — so their 8B cycle counts are simply 1.6x the 4B counts, which is the element ratio (4096/2560). The vd4dots stage is the one place the models differ: 0.155 vs 0.138 cyc/elem (+12%), which accounts for the whole 11.23x-vs-12.34x gap.

build8B cyc/elem4B cyc/elemΔ
pristine1.7351.707+1.6%
repack0.8290.818+1.3%
+ prefetch0.5290.528+0.2%
+ vd4dots (F9)0.1550.138+11.7%

Elements per node: 8B 4096×1024, 4B 2560×1024; nrows=2 in both, so per-activation numbers are these values halved.

appendix

Run environment and verification
  • Model: Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf, 1.16 GB — qwen3, 36 layers, n_embd 4096, n_head_kv 8.
  • Engine: vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 — VLEN 1024, ELEN 64, real L3 RTL.
  • Builds: bin-pristine (REPACK=OFF) · bin-baseline (REPACK=ON, PF=0) · bin-prefetch (PF=1) · bin-d4 (PF=1, Q1_D4=1, includes the F9 vsetvli batching).

  • Reproducibility: vsim is deterministic; these node counts are repeat-stable.
  • Throughput tip: runs are independent (per-run temp dirs and shm files), so the four measurements ran in parallel; the slowest (pristine, ~7.3M RTL cycles) sets the wall time.
  • Logs: ~/tmp/8b-runs/8b-hybrid-{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k51.log

# Running Bonsai-8B on andesim hybrid: 2 flags, 0 rebuilds, 11.23x

2026-08-04, engine `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (VLEN 1024, ELEN 64, real L3 RTL).
The 4B flow extends to the 8B model with two flags and no rebuild, and the
Q1_0 optimization chain gives **7,278,168 -> 648,246 cycles = 11.23x** on the
K=51 node (layer 7 V projection, `blk.7.attn_v.weight [4096 x 1024]`, nrows=2).

## Part 1 - what must change to run the 8B model

The 4B recipe carries over unchanged: same four binaries, same engine, same
ROI marker at K=51. The model file is a runtime argument. Only two flags are
new, and both exist because the 8B model presses against the 2 GiB guest RAM
window.

- **`--mem-size 2097148K`** (andesim flag). The exact hybrid maximum:
  2 GiB minus the 4 KiB hybrid scratch area. Hybrid mode rejects `2G`
  outright (only fast mode accepts it), so this literal value is required.
- **`--no-mmap`** (llama.cpp flag). On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack buffer type
  accepts these tensors, so with mmap the 1,099 MiB file mapping AND the
  931 MiB repack buffer are both resident at load time. Together with the
  other buffers that exceeds the window. `--no-mmap` drops the mapping;
  everything else fits with 565 MiB to spare.

Guest RAM demand at load, drawn to scale (1 char = 64 MiB):

```
              0    512  1024 1536 2048 = the 2 GiB window
              |----|----|----|----|
default (mmap) MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMRRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO   2,582 MiB: FAILS, 534 over
with --no-mmap RRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO                    1,483 MiB: fits, 565 free
              |----|----|----|----|
M = file mapping 1,099   R = repack buffer 931
O = other 552 (non-repacked weights 168 + KV cache 72 at -c 512 + compute 312)
```

Removing the file mapping is the whole fix: the repacked copy is the one the
kernels read, so the mapping was pure duplication.

The full command (the two 8B flags are the only changes vs 4B):

```bash
cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

<details>
<summary>Why the binaries need no rebuild</summary>

The ROI marker counts MUL_MAT nodes, not shapes. Bonsai-8B is the same qwen3
architecture as 4B (36 layers, 253 MUL_MAT per token), so compiled-in K=51
lands on the same node: the layer-7 V projection. Only its shape grows,
2560x1024 -> 4096x1024. Each run self-reports the node, so this is checked,
not assumed:

```
[roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [4096 x 1024] nrows=2
```

The repack gate also passes untouched: 1024 output rows, 1024 mod 64 = 0.

</details>

## Part 2 - speedup on the 8B node

Same optimization chain as 4B, measured on the K=51 node (RTL cycles).
Every stage keeps output bit-exact.

RTL cycles, drawn to scale (1 char = 150k cycles):

```
pristine   #################################################  7,278,168   1.00x
repack     #######################                            3,475,147   2.09x
+prefetch  ###############                                    2,218,540   3.28x
+vd4dots   ####                                                 648,246  11.23x
```

| build          | cycles    | step  | total speedup | 4B total (ref) |
|----------------|-----------|-------|---------------|----------------|
| pristine       | 7,278,168 | -     | 1.00x         | 1.00x          |
| repack         | 3,475,147 | 2.09x | 2.09x         | 2.09x          |
| + prefetch     | 2,218,540 | 1.57x | 3.28x         | 3.23x          |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 648,246   | 3.42x | **11.23x**    | 12.34x         |

The chain transfers to 8B almost exactly. Repack and prefetch cost the same
cycles per element as on 4B - the prefetch stage lands at 0.264 cyc/elem/act,
inside the 0.261-0.265 band measured across all five 4B shapes - so their 8B
cycle counts are simply 1.6x the 4B counts, which is the element ratio
(4096/2560). The vd4dots stage is the one place the models differ: 0.155 vs
0.138 cyc/elem (+12%), which accounts for the whole 11.23x-vs-12.34x gap.

<details>
<summary>Per-element comparison, 8B vs 4B</summary>

| build          | 8B cyc/elem | 4B cyc/elem | delta  |
|----------------|-------------|-------------|--------|
| pristine       | 1.735       | 1.707       | +1.6%  |
| repack         | 0.829       | 0.818       | +1.3%  |
| + prefetch     | 0.529       | 0.528       | +0.2%  |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 0.155       | 0.138       | +11.7% |

Elements per node: 8B 4096x1024, 4B 2560x1024; nrows=2 in both, so
per-activation numbers are these values halved.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Appendix - run environment and verification</summary>

- **Model**: `Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf`, 1.16 GB - qwen3, 36 layers, n_embd 4096,
  n_head_kv 8.
- **Builds**: `bin-pristine` (REPACK=OFF), `bin-baseline` (REPACK=ON, PF=0),
  `bin-prefetch` (PF=1), `bin-d4` (PF=1, Q1_D4=1, includes the F9 vsetvli
  batching).
- **Success check**: read the output, not the exit code - a good run prints
  the `[roi]` node self-check followed by `[andesim] <N> cycles`.
- **Reproducibility**: vsim is deterministic; these node counts are
  repeat-stable.
- **Throughput tip**: runs are independent (per-run temp dirs and shm files),
  so the four measurements ran in parallel; the slowest (pristine, ~7.3M RTL
  cycles) sets the wall time.
- **Logs**: `~/tmp/8b-runs/8b-hybrid-{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k51.log`

</details>

content.content:
1019	## U10. Platform track: guest RAM > 2 GiB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]
1020	
1021	Rescoped 2026-07-29 after measuring the real blockers. The original U10 text
1022	said three things that are now wrong or answered:
1023	- (1) "qemu_andesim DRAM window (currently Cannot model more than 2GB)" is
1024	  **DONE upstream**. `hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:73,131,132` now defines
1025	  `DRAM` 0x0 +2 GiB, `DRAM_ALIAS` 0x8_00000000 +2 GiB (aliases DRAM), and
1026	  `DRAM_EXT` 0x8_80000000 +14 GiB; the error at :1814-1823 reads "Cannot
1027	  model more than 16GB RAM". :974-981 auto-enables the alias when
1028	  `ram_size > DRAM.size` precisely so ext RAM is reachable **contiguously
1029	  from 0x8_00000000**, and :1837-1850 maps ONE `machine->ram` backend across
1030	  both windows via aliases -- so hybrid's `memory-backend-file` already
1031	  spans them. Nothing to do in QEMU.
1032	- (2) "is the vsim testbench memory parameterizable?" -> **yes, in hybrid
1033	  mode it already is.** `vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:458-465`: when
1034	  `--shared-mem-path` is given, the RAM region is exactly
1035	  `{shared_mem_base, shared_mem_base + shared_mem_size - 1}` with no
1036	  hardcoded 2 GiB. `SimpleMemory<BusWidth>` (src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:14-18)
1037	  takes 32 = bus width in BYTES, not address bits; addresses are u64
1038	  throughout. So the vsim side likely needs NO code change -- U10a verifies.
1039	- (3) "the vlinux arena bounds (already mem_size-driven)" is **the actual
1040	  bug, not a non-issue.** mem_size-driven means mem_size is used as an
1041	  ABSOLUTE ADDRESS, which is only correct while RAM base == 0.
1042	
1043	MEASURED 2026-07-29 (`--mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 3G`, Bonsai-8B):
1044	the guest dies **before the app's first instruction** -- no `llama backend
1045	init`, not even the startup `vlinux: ENOSYS 258/435/220`. One complete
1046	`mcause=0x2 mepc=0x0 mtval=0x0`, then 1,196,874 truncated `mcause=0x`
1047	fragments (11 MB) because the trap handler re-faults on the same broken
1048	stack. Cause: stack.c puts the initial stack at `mem_size - 8 MiB` =
1049	0xBF80_0000, which is unmapped hole in AE350 (RAM ends at 0x7FFF_FFFF, ext
1050	starts at 0x8_80000000). QEMU swallows the stores, the first return reads
1051	back 0, the hart jumps to 0. So today's fast-mode behaviour for >2 GiB is a
1052	CPU-burning trap storm, not an error -- see U10b.
1053	
1054	Target: `--mem-size 6G` in both fast and hybrid, Bonsai-27B-Q1_0 (3.8 GB)
1055	resident with NO `--no-mmap` and no layer slicing (obsoletes U11's need).
1056	8 GiB is enough for 27B; the ceiling the map allows is 16 GiB.
1057	
1058	### U10a. Probe: does the RTL decode 0x8_00000000? [DONE 2026-07-29 -- answer: NO]
1059	
1060	- Description: throwaway investigation, NOT code -- one command, read the
1061	  answer, write it down here. (Avoid the word "spike" for this in a RISC-V
1062	  repo: it reads as the Spike ISA simulator, which is not involved.)
1063	- RESULT: **the high window is NOT reachable on any engine we use.** Two
1064	  layers disagree and only one of them is the truth:
1065	  - `--print-memmap` HAPPILY accepts any base/size, which is MISLEADING --
1066	    it dumps the SystemC/TLM `interconnect` region table, a C++ map, not an
1067	    RTL capability. Measured: `--shared-mem-base 0x800000000
1068	    --shared-mem-size 4G` -> `main_memory.tsck: [0x800000000-0x8ffffffff]`;
1069	    at 16G -> `[0x800000000-0xbffffffff]`. Both "pass". Do not trust this
1070	    output alone for an addressability question.
1071	  - The engine config tells the truth:
1072	    `vsim_andesim/data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg:291
1073	    set o(NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH) {32}` (and :295 `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH {32}`).
1074	    The core's bus interface drives 32-bit physical addresses, so
1075	    0x8_00000000 (36 bits) can never be issued no matter what the TLM map
1076	    says. `SimpleMemory::base_for()` subtracts the region base to index the
1077	    mmap, so a 32-bit address against a 0x8_00000000 region matches nothing.
1078	- It IS a per-elaboration knob, not an architectural limit: same repo,
1079	  `ax45mp.cfg` = 38, `ax65.cfg` / `ax66_makatau.cfg` / `ax66_mp2.cfg` = 39.
1080	  Every ax45mpv_premium* and ax46mpv* variant we have is 32.
1081	- Second ceiling, independent of the BIU: even using the full 32-bit space,
1082	  the vsim platform puts HVM at 0x9000_0000, slv_bridge at 0xa000_0000,
1083	  PLDM at 0xe680_0000, smu/uart at 0xf01-0xf03. RAM can therefore only grow
1084	  from 0x8000_0000 to 0x8fff_ffff = **+256 MiB (2.25 GiB total)** before
1085	  colliding. Enough to make 8B work WITH mmap (it missed by ~1 MiB: 1099
1086	  mapping + 931 repack + ~10 app + 8 stack reserve vs a 2047 MiB cap), never
1087	  enough for 27B.
1088	- CONSEQUENCE: U10d/U10e as originally written (rebase guest RAM to
1089	  0x8_00000000) are DEAD for hybrid. U10 splits into two tracks with very
1090	  different costs -- see U10-FAST and U10-HYBRID below.
1091	- Key files: vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp, data/configs/*.cfg (read only)
1092	- State: DONE
1093	
1094	### U10b. Fix the missing fast-mode --mem-size guard [independent bug]

## U10. Platform track: guest RAM > 2 GiB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]

Rescoped 2026-07-29 after measuring the real blockers. The original U10 text
said three things that are now wrong or answered:
- (1) "qemu_andesim DRAM window (currently Cannot model more than 2GB)" is
  **DONE upstream**. `hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:73,131,132` now defines
  `DRAM` 0x0 +2 GiB, `DRAM_ALIAS` 0x8_00000000 +2 GiB (aliases DRAM), and
  `DRAM_EXT` 0x8_80000000 +14 GiB; the error at :1814-1823 reads "Cannot
  model more than 16GB RAM". :974-981 auto-enables the alias when
  `ram_size > DRAM.size` precisely so ext RAM is reachable **contiguously
  from 0x8_00000000**, and :1837-1850 maps ONE `machine->ram` backend across
  both windows via aliases -- so hybrid's `memory-backend-file` already
  spans them. Nothing to do in QEMU.
- (2) "is the vsim testbench memory parameterizable?" -> **yes, in hybrid
  mode it already is.** `vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:458-465`: when
  `--shared-mem-path` is given, the RAM region is exactly
  `{shared_mem_base, shared_mem_base + shared_mem_size - 1}` with no
  hardcoded 2 GiB. `SimpleMemory<BusWidth>` (src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:14-18)
  takes 32 = bus width in BYTES, not address bits; addresses are u64
  throughout. So the vsim side likely needs NO code change -- U10a verifies.
- (3) "the vlinux arena bounds (already mem_size-driven)" is **the actual
  bug, not a non-issue.** mem_size-driven means mem_size is used as an
  ABSOLUTE ADDRESS, which is only correct while RAM base == 0.

MEASURED 2026-07-29 (`--mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 3G`, Bonsai-8B):
the guest dies **before the app's first instruction** -- no `llama backend
init`, not even the startup `vlinux: ENOSYS 258/435/220`. One complete
`mcause=0x2 mepc=0x0 mtval=0x0`, then 1,196,874 truncated `mcause=0x`
fragments (11 MB) because the trap handler re-faults on the same broken
stack. Cause: stack.c puts the initial stack at `mem_size - 8 MiB` =
0xBF80_0000, which is unmapped hole in AE350 (RAM ends at 0x7FFF_FFFF, ext
starts at 0x8_80000000). QEMU swallows the stores, the first return reads
back 0, the hart jumps to 0. So today's fast-mode behaviour for >2 GiB is a
CPU-burning trap storm, not an error -- see U10b.

Target: `--mem-size 6G` in both fast and hybrid, Bonsai-27B-Q1_0 (3.8 GB)
resident with NO `--no-mmap` and no layer slicing (obsoletes U11's need).
8 GiB is enough for 27B; the ceiling the map allows is 16 GiB.

### U10a. Probe: does the RTL decode 0x8_00000000? [DONE 2026-07-29 -- answer: NO]

- Description: throwaway investigation, NOT code -- one command, read the
  answer, write it down here. (Avoid the word "spike" for this in a RISC-V
  repo: it reads as the Spike ISA simulator, which is not involved.)
- RESULT: **the high window is NOT reachable on any engine we use.** Two
  layers disagree and only one of them is the truth:
  - `--print-memmap` HAPPILY accepts any base/size, which is MISLEADING --
    it dumps the SystemC/TLM `interconnect` region table, a C++ map, not an
    RTL capability. Measured: `--shared-mem-base 0x800000000
    --shared-mem-size 4G` -> `main_memory.tsck: [0x800000000-0x8ffffffff]`;
    at 16G -> `[0x800000000-0xbffffffff]`. Both "pass". Do not trust this
    output alone for an addressability question.
  - The engine config tells the truth:
    `vsim_andesim/data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg:291
    set o(NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH) {32}` (and :295 `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH {32}`).
    The core's bus interface drives 32-bit physical addresses, so
    0x8_00000000 (36 bits) can never be issued no matter what the TLM map
    says. `SimpleMemory::base_for()` subtracts the region base to index the
    mmap, so a 32-bit address against a 0x8_00000000 region matches nothing.
- It IS a per-elaboration knob, not an architectural limit: same repo,
  `ax45mp.cfg` = 38, `ax65.cfg` / `ax66_makatau.cfg` / `ax66_mp2.cfg` = 39.
  Every ax45mpv_premium* and ax46mpv* variant we have is 32.
- Second ceiling, independent of the BIU: even using the full 32-bit space,
  the vsim platform puts HVM at 0x9000_0000, slv_bridge at 0xa000_0000,
  PLDM at 0xe680_0000, smu/uart at 0xf01-0xf03. RAM can therefore only grow
  from 0x8000_0000 to 0x8fff_ffff = **+256 MiB (2.25 GiB total)** before
  colliding. Enough to make 8B work WITH mmap (it missed by ~1 MiB: 1099
  mapping + 931 repack + ~10 app + 8 stack reserve vs a 2047 MiB cap), never
  enough for 27B.
- CONSEQUENCE: U10d/U10e as originally written (rebase guest RAM to
  0x8_00000000) are DEAD for hybrid. U10 splits into two tracks with very
  different costs -- see U10-FAST and U10-HYBRID below.
- Key files: vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp, data/configs/*.cfg (read only)
- State: DONE

  to runtime/linux/Makefile's HDRS so edits trigger a rebuild.

### U10d. Manifest v3: carry ram_base, vlinux computes ram_base + mem_size

- Description: BEHAVIOURAL. `struct vlinux_manifest` (runtime/linux/manifest.h)
  is version 2 with `magic/version/mem_size/app_path/argv_*`; add
  `uint64_t ram_base` and bump `VLINUX_MANIFEST_VERSION` to 3. Every function
  extracted in U10c takes ram_base and returns `ram_base + mem_size`-relative
  addresses. Land it with the driver still writing ram_base = 0, so behaviour
  is provably identical -- the switch to a non-zero base is U10e. Note the
  app image and vlinux itself do NOT need relinking: they live below
  0x0220_0000 and 0x8_00000000 aliases those same physical bytes, so only the
  mmap arena and the initial stack move. brk stays low (its ceiling is
  `_vlinux_base`, 32 MiB), which is fine -- the arenas never need to adjoin.
- Input/Output: RED = a test asserting the arena top for
  (ram_base=0x800000000, mem_size=4G) is 0x8_FF80_0000; manifest_test.cpp
  pins version 3 + the new field; 4B smoke byte-identical output.
- Key files: runtime/linux/manifest.h, mm.c, stack.c, loader.c,
  driver/manifest.cpp, driver/manifest_test.cpp
- Depends on: U10c.
- **State: DONE 2026-07-29.** `struct vlinux_manifest` gained
  `uint64_t ram_base` (APPENDED, so `VLINUX_MANIFEST_VERSION` 2 -> 3: a v2
  reader would mis-parse). Threaded through three signatures --
  `mm_init(app_image_end, ram_base, mem_size)`,
  `build_initial_stack(app_path, ram_base, mem_size, ...)`,
  `load_elf(path, ram_base, mem_size, out)` -- plus
  `build_manifest_blob(app_path, mem_size, ram_base, extra_argv, err)` and
  `stage_linux_runtime(app_elf, mem_size, ram_base, extra_argv, err)` on the
  driver side. main.c snapshots the field alongside mem_size and passes it on.
  RED confirmed first (`'struct vlinux_manifest' has no member named
  'ram_base'`). **The driver still passes a literal 0** at
  cmd_run.cpp's stage_linux_boot, so the guest layout is byte-for-byte v2's --
  flipping it on is U10e/U10f. 14/14 driver tests green; vlinux.elf and the
  driver both rebuild warning-free.

### U10e. FAST-MODE TRACK: >2 GiB in fast mode [achievable now, no RTL]

- Description: BEHAVIOURAL. **This track is unblocked by U10a's finding**
  because fast mode has NO vsim leg -- QEMU's TCG addresses the full 16 GiB
  map, so `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH` is irrelevant here. Fast mode already skips the
  hybrid cap (cmd_run.cpp:246-252, which is U10b's bug); once the runtime
  honours ram_base (U10d) the driver can hand fast mode
  `ram_base = 0x8_00000000` and any size up to DRAM + DRAM_EXT = 16 GiB.
  Nothing in shm.cpp / run_plan.hpp / memmap.cpp needs to change -- those are
  the hybrid transport. Scope this to `--mode fast --runtime linux` only and
  keep hybrid at its current ceiling.
- Value: unlocks the whole 27B *correctness* story with no RTL work --
  functional runs, bit-exactness A/Bs, output diffs at full model size. Only
  cycle measurement stays capped. Also obsoletes U11 (layer slicing) for
  everything except hybrid.
- Input/Output: `--mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 6G` boots and runs;
  U10b's ceiling for fast becomes 16 GiB while hybrid's stays 2 GiB, so the
  two modes now legitimately differ and the error messages must say which.
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp (fast path only), driver/manifest.cpp,
  driver/run_test.cpp
- Depends on: U10c, U10d. NOT on U10a.
- State: PLANNED

### U10f. HYBRID TRACK: >2 GiB under vsim [BLOCKED on a re-elaborated engine]

- Description: needs a new engine whose `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH` (and
  `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH`) reach >= 36 bits, then the driver changes that were
  originally U10e: (a) `driver/shm.cpp:90-94` `max_program_mem_bytes()` 2 GiB
  -> the new ceiling; (b) `driver/run_plan.hpp:27` `mmap_base = "0x0"` ->
  0x8_00000000 when mem > 2 GiB (already plumbed as the `{mmap_base}`
  placeholder, a one-value change); (c) `driver/memmap.cpp:93` V-scratch gpa
  becomes ram_base + program_bytes. Existing tests PIN the old values and are
  the RED step: `infra_test.cpp:55-60` asserts `max_program_mem_bytes() ==
  2 GiB - scratch`; `plan_test.cpp:95,152,481` assert
  `"--shared-mem-base","0x0"`.
- Engine work: the build flow is `config.yaml` entry -> RTL package + a
  `data/configs/*.cfg` -> config tool -> Verilator (`config.yaml:46-53`:
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3 = package `ax46mpv_advanced` + its cfg +
  `--threads 8 --unroll-count 256`). Precedent: premium_max was made exactly
  this way (2026-07-23, ELEN/FELEN 64 + PACKED_FP16 + D$ 32K). The config
  step is standalone and cheap to test without Verilator
  (cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake:73-87):
  `NDS_HOME=<tree> tclsh <tree>/config_tools/nds-softcore-config --load <cfg> --generate`

- **GATE 1 PASSED 2026-07-29: the config tool accepts a wide BIU.**
  Probed on a throwaway copy of external/ax46mpv_advanced (94 MB) in
  /home/nick/tmp, leaving the real engines untouched; a control run with the
  unmodified cfg passed first, so the environment was known-good.
  `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH 32 -> 39` + `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH 32 -> 39` -> exit 0,
  "Finished customizing IP", and config.inc gets
  `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH 39` / `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH 39`.
  - Values are NOT free-form. `nds-softcore-config:6435`
    `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH value {32 37 38 39 52 59 64}` (enum -- 36 is
    REJECTED: "ERROR: 36 is not a valid option value of L3-Cache Address
    Width"), while `:4363-4368` `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH` is `textinput` 32-64,
    tool default 39. Pick from the L3C enum; 39 matches ax65/ax66 and the
    tool's own default.
  - **The tool auto-widens 6 dependent RAM/tag widths, which VALIDATES
    regenerating over hand-editing.** Full config.inc diff at 32 vs 39, all
    +7: STLB_RAM_DW 60->67, STLB_DATA_RAM_DW 30->37, ICACHE_TAG_RAM_DW
    30->37, DCACHE_TAG_RAM_DW 32->39, CM_SNP_RAM_DW 21->28, L3C_TAG_RAM_DW
    18->25. Hand-patching the two cfg lines (or config.inc directly) would
    leave TLB and cache tags too narrow to hold a full address -- silent
    corruption, not a build error.
- **GATE 2 PASSED 2026-07-29: the widened engine builds AND is timing-neutral.**
  Done in place on `data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg` (BIU 32->39, L3C 32->39)
  + `./build_vsim.sh`, at the user's direction. The rebuild is incremental --
  only this engine's config changed, so the other 6 are skipped; the previous
  binary was preserved as `build/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.biu32-backup` before
  building, since build_vsim.sh overwrites in place.
  - `build/Vax46mpv_fpga_l3/obj_sc/config.inc` confirms the widened defines
    reached the elaborated RTL: BIU 39, L3C 39, plus the auto-widened
    STLB_RAM_DW 67 / DCACHE_TAG_RAM_DW 39 / L3C_TAG_RAM_DW 25.
  - **TIMING-NEUTRAL, controlled A/B**: same bin-prefetch, 4B K=51 node ->
    BIU=39 engine 1,384,130 cycles, BIU=32 backup engine **1,384,130** --
    bit-identical. (Staged the backup in its own dir and pointed
    `VSIM_BIN_DIR` at it; driver/engine_registry.cpp:186 honours that env.)
    Expected, since tag-RAM width does not change cache sets/ways or TLB
    entry count. So every cycle number measured on the old engine remains
    comparable, and this widening is safe to keep permanently.
  - Byproduct worth keeping: a REBUILD of unchanged llama.cpp source drifts
    ~0.37% (recorded 1,389,236 -> rebuilt 1,384,130). The A/B above isolates
    that to the binary, NOT the engine. Any scaling/A-B claim must use
    binaries from one build session.
- REMAINING GATES:
  3. The elaborated core actually ISSUES a >32-bit address, i.e. a load/store
     to 0x8_00000000 reaches main_memory. `--print-memmap` CANNOT answer this
     (U10a): it prints the TLM region table and gave byte-identical output on
     the BIU=32 and BIU=39 engines. A real access requires the guest to place
     data up there, which requires a non-zero ram_base --
     **so gate 3 is BLOCKED ON U10d, not on the engine.** (Dependency
     corrected 2026-07-29; the earlier "depends on an engine rebuild" was
     incomplete.)
  4. The vsim testbench may need matching work: `testbench/ae350_system.v`
     and `testbench/ae350_tb.sv` also reference NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH. Note
     ae350_system.v:155,165,707 already derive their widths FROM the define
     (so they widened automatically), while e.g. :288
     `wire [31:0] H_hs0_haddr_32b` is a deliberately 32-bit AHB signal. No
     width errors surfaced in this build, but nothing has driven a wide
     address through the platform yet -- gate 3 is what would expose it.
- Note a wide BIU also disposes of the device-collision problem: RAM moves
  above the platform windows (HVM 0x9000_0000, slv_bridge 0xa000_0000, PLDM
  0xe680_0000, smu/uart 0xf01-0xf03 all stay put). Staying inside 32 bits
  instead buys only +256 MiB (see U10a) and is not worth doing.
- Input/Output: a new engine in `config.yaml` whose `--print-memmap` shows
  RAM at 0x8_00000000 AND which actually executes a load/store there;
  `--mode hybrid --mem-size 6G` measures a 27B ROI.
- Key files: vsim_andesim/config.yaml, vsim_andesim/data/configs/*.cfg,
  driver/shm.cpp, driver/run_plan.hpp, driver/memmap.cpp + the test files above
- Depends on: U10c, U10d (gate 3 cannot even be TESTED without ram_base
  support). The engine rebuild is DONE and was cheap; the remaining cost and
  risk sit in the runtime work, not the RTL.
- State: engine ready (gates 1-2 passed); gate 3 BLOCKED on U10d

- Status: PARKED - only matters when 27B comes back in scope, which also

  edge case only the 27B tensor sizes hit.

  generic C or fp16 ABI; (2) bisect op-level with llama-eval-callback host
  vs QEMU, find first divergent op; (3) fix + add the failing shape to
  test-backend-ops.

## What the try showed

functions in runtime/linux/vlinux_mem.h (vlinux_ram_top, vlinux_mmap_arena_top,
vlinux_v_scratch_base); VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE moves there so mm.c and stack.c
structurally cannot desynchronize. New driver/vlinux_mem_test.cpp (14th driver
test) pins today's ram_base==0 answers and encodes the 3G trap-storm bug as an
assertion on the unmapped-hole address.

threaded through mm_init, build_initial_stack, load_elf, build_manifest_blob,
stage_linux_runtime. The driver still passes ram_base = 0, so the guest layout
is byte-for-byte v2's - flipping it on is U10e/U10f.

Also: docs updates (USER_GUIDE, llama_roi_howto) and
scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh, the documented K=51 hybrid example runner.

14/14 driver unit tests green.

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  cmd_profile.cpp
  profile.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  log.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  vsim_filter.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
  memmap.cpp
  manifest.cpp
  tempdir.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp tempdir.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp engine_registry.cpp tempdir.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# cycle-mode output filter: banner/[info] suppression + cycle-count lift (pure).
add_executable(andesim-vsimfilter-test vsim_filter_test.cpp vsim_filter.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andesim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andesim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp log.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andesim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
# EX1: vsim scan dir picks $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim, mirrors $QEMU_BIN_DIR).
add_executable(andesim-engine-registry-test engine_registry_test.cpp engine_registry.cpp process.cpp)
# hybrid guest memory-map composer (pure; descriptor + qemu.cfg text in, rows out).
add_executable(andesim-memmap-test memmap_test.cpp memmap.cpp)
# profile core: plugin-log/disasm parsing, RVV filter, loop nesting, renderers,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build this repo's vsim inside the Dockerfile's env-stage container image.
#
# What it does (README Option 3):
#   1. Build the `env` target image (verilator + toolchain) from ./Dockerfile.
#   2. Run ./build.sh inside that container with the repo bind-mounted at /work,
#      so build artifacts land in ./build/ on the host.
#
# Trim config.yaml to the CPU(s) you need first to cut build time.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Container runtime: prefer podman, fall back to docker.
if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=podman
elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=docker
else
  echo "error: need podman or docker on PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "error: missing $ROOT/Dockerfile" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# build.sh / cmake pull in external/ submodules; bail early if they are empty.
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/external/fmt/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
  echo "error: submodules not initialized - run:" >&2
  echo "  git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"

"$RUNTIME" build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
"$RUNTIME" run --rm \
  -v "$ROOT:/work" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

same file offsets. Legacy runs (base 0) keep the single-region map and
measure bit-identical (4B K=51: 362,799 before and after).

EOF
)" && git log -1 --oneline

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Align two eval-callback dumps by node order; report the first divergence.

A node is `common_debug_cb_eval: <name> = (<ty>) <OP>(...) = {shape}` followed
(after the value block) by `sum = <float>`. fp reassociation across arches is
normal; only order-of-magnitude relative gaps or NaN count as divergence.
"""
import re
import sys

HDR = re.compile(r'common_debug_cb_eval:\s+(\S+) = \((\w+)\)\s+(\w+)\(')
SUM = re.compile(r'^\s*sum = (\S+)')


def parse(path):
    nodes = []
    name = None
    with open(path, errors='replace') as f:
        for line in f:
            m = HDR.search(line)
            if m:
                name = (m.group(1), m.group(3))  # (tensor name, OP)
                continue
            m = SUM.match(line)
            if m and name is not None:
                nodes.append((name[0], name[1], float(m.group(1))))
                name = None
    return nodes


def main(host_path, rvv_path, rel_tol=0.05, abs_floor=1.0):
    h, r = parse(host_path), parse(rvv_path)
    print(f'host nodes: {len(h)}   rvv nodes: {len(r)}')
    n = min(len(h), len(r))
    shown = 0
    for i in range(n):
        hn, ho, hs = h[i]
        rn, ro, rs = r[i]
        if hn != rn or ho != ro:
            print(f'[{i}] GRAPH MISMATCH host={hn}/{ho} rvv={rn}/{ro}')
            return
        bad = (rs != rs) or (hs != hs)  # NaN
        if not bad:
            denom = max(abs(hs), abs_floor)
            bad = abs(hs - rs) / denom > rel_tol
        if bad:
            print(f'[{i}] {ho:14s} {hn:50s} host={hs:<18.6f} rvv={rs:<18.6f}')
            shown += 1
            if shown >= 25:
                print('... (more suppressed)')
                return
    if shown == 0:
        print('no divergence above tolerance')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Align two eval-callback dumps by node order; report the first divergence.

A node is `common_debug_cb_eval: <name> = (<ty>) <OP>(...) = {shape}` followed
(after the value block) by `sum = <float>`. fp reassociation across arches is
normal; only order-of-magnitude relative gaps or NaN count as divergence.
"""
import re
import sys

HDR = re.compile(r'common_debug_cb_eval:\s+(\S+) = \((\w+)\)\s+(\w+)\(')
SUM = re.compile(r'^\s*sum = (\S+)')


def parse(path):
    nodes = []
    name = None
    with open(path, errors='replace') as f:
        for line in f:
            m = HDR.search(line)
            if m:
                name = (m.group(1), m.group(3))  # (tensor name, OP)
                continue
            m = SUM.match(line)
            if m and name is not None:
                nodes.append((name[0], name[1], float(m.group(1))))
                name = None
    return nodes


def main(host_path, rvv_path, rel_tol=0.05, abs_floor=1.0):
    h, r = parse(host_path), parse(rvv_path)
    print(f'host nodes: {len(h)}   rvv nodes: {len(r)}')
    n = min(len(h), len(r))
    shown = 0
    for i in range(n):
        hn, ho, hs = h[i]
        rn, ro, rs = r[i]
        if hn != rn or ho != ro:
            print(f'[{i}] GRAPH MISMATCH host={hn}/{ho} rvv={rn}/{ro}')
            return
        bad = (rs != rs) or (hs != hs)  # NaN
        if not bad:
            denom = max(abs(hs), abs_floor)
            bad = abs(hs - rs) / denom > rel_tol
        if bad:
            print(f'[{i}] {ho:14s} {hn:50s} host={hs:<18.6f} rvv={rs:<18.6f}')
            shown += 1
            if shown >= 25:
                print('... (more suppressed)')
                return
    if shown == 0:
        print('no divergence above tolerance')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

**Bonsai-8B WORKS on hybrid AND fast (2026-07-29)** - models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf
(1158654496 B, byte-size-identical to HF prism-ml/Bonsai-8B-gguf, already local).
qwen3, 36 layers (same as 4B), n_embd 4096, n_head_kv 8. Two flags that are NOT
in build.sh/measure.sh/verify.sh defaults and are both mandatory:
- **`--no-mmap`**: without it the load dies at 54s with `ggml_aligned_malloc:
  insufficient memory (attempted to allocate 931.50 MB)` /
  `failed to allocate CPU_REPACK buffer of size 976748544`. Root cause: on RISC-V
  the Q1_0 repack buft ACCEPTS these tensors (on x86 it is rejected -> mmap only),
  so the 1099 MiB file mapping AND the 931 MiB CPU_REPACK buffer are both resident
  = 2030 MiB > the 2 GiB window. vlinux implements mmap (only ENOSYS 258
  riscv_hwprobe / 435 clone3 / 220 clone), so the mapping really costs guest RAM.
  With --no-mmap: 931 (repack) + ~168 (rest) + 72 (KV @ -c 512) + 312 (compute @
  n_batch 2048) = ~1484 MiB, fits. Further headroom if ever needed: -b 512, -c 256.
- **`--mem-size 2097148K`** = the exact hybrid max (2 GiB - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES,
  = 32*128 = 4096 B; include/hybrid/state_abi.h:73,80 + driver/shm.cpp:90).
  hybrid REJECTS `2G` with "exceeds the AE350 DRAM window" - it does not silently
  cap. fast mode accepts `2G` because it goes straight to QEMU `-m` (main.cpp:78),
  so the two modes have DIFFERENT --mem-size rules.
8B hybrid FULL CHAIN (2026-08-04, fpga_l3, K=51 = blk.7.attn_v.weight
[4096 x 1024] nrows=2, logs /home/nick/tmp/8b-runs/): pristine 7,278,168 ->
repack 3,475,147 (2.09x) -> +prefetch 2,218,540 (3.28x) -> d4/F9 648,246
(**11.23x**). Repack and prefetch stages scale per-element 1:1 from 4B
(prefetch 0.264 cyc/elem/act, inside the 0.261-0.265 invariant band); d4 is
the only stage that degrades: 0.155 vs 0.138 cyc/elem on 4B (~12%), so 8B
total is 11.23x vs 4B 12.34x - "decode purely issue-bound" starts to crack
at K=4096 (unverified why; more weight bytes streamed per row).
Exit codes: a SUCCESSFUL fast-mode run returns **2** (the generic vlinux exit trap
at RAM-top; mepc tracks --mem-size: 0x7cfffdc2 at 2000M, 0x7ffffdd2 at 2G). hybrid
returns 0 because nothing runs after the ROI. So exit code is NOT a success signal
in either mode - grep the output. Wall clock: 8B fast mode 8 tokens = ~23 min.

**BIU/L3C address width widened to 39 on ax46mpv_fpga_l3, 2026-07-29 - and it is
TIMING-NEUTRAL.** Motivation: reaching QEMU's DRAM_EXT window needs >32-bit
physical addresses (see the andesim ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U10 rewrite).
- `data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg`: `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH` and
  `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH` 32 -> 39, rebuilt via `./build_vsim.sh` (incremental:
  only this engine re-verilates, the other 6 configs are untouched so ninja
  skips them). Old binary preserved as
  `build/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.biu32-backup`.
- Value RULES (`external/ax46mpv_advanced/config_tools/nds-softcore-config`):
  :6435 `NDS_L3C_ADDR_WIDTH value {32 37 38 39 52 59 64}` is an ENUM - 36 is
  rejected ("ERROR: 36 is not a valid option value of L3-Cache Address Width");
  :4363-4368 `NDS_BIU_ADDR_WIDTH` is free `textinput` 32-64, tool default 39.
- The config tool AUTO-WIDENS 6 dependent widths (all +7): STLB_RAM_DW 60->67,
  STLB_DATA_RAM_DW 30->37, ICACHE_TAG_RAM_DW 30->37, DCACHE_TAG_RAM_DW 32->39,
  CM_SNP_RAM_DW 21->28, L3C_TAG_RAM_DW 18->25. So NEVER hand-patch config.inc
  or a single cfg line - narrow TLB/cache tags would silently truncate
  addresses. Always regenerate (the standalone step is
  `NDS_HOME=<tree> tclsh <tree>/config_tools/nds-softcore-config --load <cfg> --generate`).
- **TIMING NEUTRAL, PROVEN**: same bin-prefetch, 4B K=51 node, BIU=39 engine
  1,384,130 cycles vs BIU=32 backup engine 1,384,130 - bit-identical, not
  "close". Expected: tag-RAM WIDTH does not change cache sets/ways or TLB entry
  count. Controlled A/B done by staging the backup in its own dir and pointing
  `VSIM_BIN_DIR` at it (driver/engine_registry.cpp:186 honours that env).
  Consequence: every cycle number recorded on the old engine stays comparable.
- STILL UNVERIFIED: whether the widened core actually ISSUES a >32-bit address.
  `--print-memmap` CANNOT answer it - it prints the SystemC/TLM region table and
  happily accepted `--shared-mem-base 0x800000000` even on the BIU=32 engine
  (identical output before and after the rebuild). A real load/store up there
  needs vlinux to place its arenas at a non-zero ram_base = roadmap U10d, so
  U10f's "does the RTL address it" gate is BLOCKED ON U10d, not only on the
  engine rebuild.

content.text:
**Miscompile caught red-handed in the disassembly.** The failing `ggml_vec_dot_f32`:

```asm
 2: vsetvli a4,zero,e32,m8,tu,ma
 6: vmv.v.i v8,0            ; vsum zeroed correctly (e32m8)
 a: vsetvli t1,zero,e8,m2,ta,ma   ; vtype switched for the m1 scalar init
 e: vmv.s.x v1,zero
12: vmv.v.i v8,0            ; !! REDONE under e8,m2,ta - zeroes only v8-v9,
                            ;    and TAIL-AGNOSTIC leaves v10-v15 undefined
```

GCC re-emitted the vsum init under the wrong vtype. Under tail-agnostic rules an implementation may fill the tail with 1s - Andes QEMU does exactly that - so 6 of the 8 accumulator registers start as garbage, and `vfredusum` sums it: the 1e19 explosion, layout-independent, build-dependent (scheduling-sensitive). The source-level sin that invites this: `__riscv_vfmv_v_f_f32m8_tu(vsum, 0.0f, vl)` **with `vsum` uninitialized** - the `_tu` merge into an indeterminate value gives GCC latitude to treat the def as movable/redundant. The zvfh `vec_dot_f16` uses the same `_tu`-on-uninitialized pattern, which explains the old-tree (zvfh) garbage too. And qwen3 4B/8B never call `vec_dot_f32`/`f16` on their decode paths (flash-attn f16 KV is scalar without zvfh; no delta-net), so every previous measurement stands.

Waiting for the dot-only probe to seal the attribution, then: revert probe scaffolding, rewrite both dot branches without the `_tu`-on-uninit pattern, verify the new object has exactly one correctly-typed init, and run the e2e GREEN.

input.new_string:
### F0. qwen35 (hybrid attention) produces garbage on rv64

- Status: **FIXED 2026-08-05.** Root cause was not a qwen35 op at all: the
  RVV `ggml_vec_dot_f32` (and the zvfh `ggml_vec_dot_f16`) initialized their
  accumulator with a `_tu` intrinsic whose merge operand was an
  UNINITIALIZED register. That value is indeterminate, so GCC 14.2 (Andes)
  was free to re-materialize the init - and did, under whatever vtype was
  current: the emitted code zeroed vsum under `e8,m2,ta`, leaving 6 of the 8
  accumulator registers tail-agnostic. QEMU implements tail-agnostic as
  all-ones, so every dot returned garbage of ~1e19 and the delta-net
  recurrence exploded (first divergent node: GATED_DELTA_NET, layer 2,
  decode path). qwen3 4B/8B never call vec_dot_f32/f16 on their decode paths
  (flash-attn f16 KV is scalar without zvfh; no delta-net), which is why
  they were always correct and every recorded cycle number stands.
  - Diagnosis: 3-way llama-eval-callback diff (x86 host / rv64 scalar /
    rv64 RVV under qemu-user) at 1 token; per-TU -march bisect (ops.cpp
    scalar -> still garbage; vec.cpp scalar -> correct); disassembly showed
    the double-init; standalone harnesses proved every helper and the
    kernel math correct in isolation (the miscompile is
    scheduling-context-sensitive).
  - Fix: plain (non-_tu) accumulator init at vlmax + plain stripe loads;
    `_tu` stays only on the accumulate, which is what preserves high-lane
    partials on the final short stripe. Verified: fixed object has a single
    correctly-typed init; 27B decode text matches x86 host at temp 0.

git status --porcelain | grep -v '^??' | head; git add ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp opt_roadmap.md && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(riscv): vec_dot f32/f16 - no _tu merge into uninitialized accumulators

The RVV branches of ggml_vec_dot_f32 (and the zvfh ggml_vec_dot_f16)
initialized their accumulator via a _tu intrinsic whose merge operand was an
uninitialized register. That operand is indeterminate, and GCC 14.2 (Andes)
re-materialized the init under whatever vtype was live at the point it chose
- observed as `vmv.v.i v8,0` under e8,m2,ta after a correct e32,m8 init,
leaving 6 of the 8 accumulator registers tail-agnostic. On implementations
that write all-ones for agnostic tails (QEMU does), every dot product came
back ~1e19 and the qwen35 delta-net recurrence exploded; first divergent
node was GATED_DELTA_NET layer 2 on the decode path. qwen3 models never call
these helpers on their decode paths, which is why 4B/8B were always correct.

Fix: plain (non-_tu) accumulator init at vlmax and plain stripe loads; _tu
remains only on the accumulate, which is what genuinely needs it (preserving
high-lane partials across the final short stripe).

RED: Bonsai-27B (qwen35) rv64 decode produced garbage ("the, is the same
for the same") while x86 host and rv64 scalar builds printed "Paris.";
per-TU -march bisect isolated vec.cpp; disassembly showed the double-init.
GREEN: fixed build prints "The capital of France is Paris." byte-equal to
host at temp 0; fixed object has a single correctly-typed init; helper unit
sweeps (n=7..16384) match scalar bit-for-bit except ULP reduction order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log -1 --oneline

content.text:
**Goal complete: Bonsai-27B runs under andesim hybrid mode, and every optimization's speedup is measured.**

## The 27B speedup chain (K=51 = `blk.6.attn_gate.weight [5120 x 6144]`, nrows=2, `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`, 6G `--no-mmap`)

| build | cycles | step | total speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| pristine | 54,314,202 | - | 1.00x |
| repack | 25,629,722 | 2.12x | 2.12x |
| + prefetch | 16,317,304 | 1.57x | 3.33x |
| + vd4dots (d4/F9) | 4,578,346 | 3.56x | **11.86x** |

Per-element costs line up with 4B/8B almost perfectly (pristine 1.73 vs 1.71/1.74 cyc/elem; repack 0.81; prefetch 0.259/act, at the edge of the invariant band; d4 0.146) - the whole optimization stack transfers to the 27B scale.

## What had to be solved, in order

1. **U10b** (andesim `5c134e5`): fast-mode `--mem-size` ceiling guard - clean error instead of a trap storm.
2. **U10e** (`1edb88d`): fast mode addresses up to 16G via `ram_base=0x8_00000000`; proven by 8B at 3G with mmap ON generating text byte-identical to the 2G control.
3. **U10f** (`9d10a6d` + vsim `e874381`): hybrid up to 16G - driver policy + a low-window alias region in vsim so the RTL fetches the low-linked code. Gate 3 passed: first real >32-bit addresses through the BIU=39 RTL; legacy 2000M measurement stayed bit-identical (362,799).
4. **F0** (llama.cpp `17b246b44`): the qwen35 rv64 garbage was a latent **`_tu`-on-uninitialized-accumulator bug in RVV `ggml_vec_dot_f32`/`f16`** - Andes GCC re-materialized the init under the wrong vtype, leaving 6 of 8 accumulator registers as tail-agnostic garbage. Found by 3-way eval-callback diffing, per-TU `-march` bisect, and disassembly; fixed with defined-value inits. The 27B now prints "The capital of France is Paris." matching x86 at temp 0, and the fixed binary reproduces the 4B chain number within 2 cycles (362,797 vs 362,799) - all previous measurements stand. This fix is upstream-worthy.

Still finishing in the background: the formal U10g(2) andesim-fast 27B text run on the fixed binary (slow under system TCG; the same proof already exists under qemu-user). Logs in `/home/nick/tmp/8b-runs/`; all work committed across the three repos.

content.text:
Two different failures - one was a real code bug (fixed in code), the newest one was my own launch mistake (fixed by correcting the command, no code change).

## The 31-hour stuck run (the one you asked about)

**Problem: memory over-budget, caused by my launch flags.** I forgot `--no-mmap`. On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack path accepts these tensors, so llama.cpp keeps BOTH copies resident during load:

| what | size |
|---|---|
| file mapping (mmap) | 3.8 G |
| repack buffer | ~3.1 G |
| KV + compute + misc | ~0.4 G |
| **total demand** | **~7.3 G** |
| window I gave it | 6 G |

Under vlinux, mmap costs real guest RAM, so this could never fit. The 8B version of this mistake fails in 54 s with a clean "insufficient memory" error - but the 27B case did not error; it ground at 99% CPU silently. I killed it after 31 h without autopsying the exact grind site, so "why slow instead of fail-fast" is recorded as an open trap in my notes, with a fail-fast guard listed as a worthwhile future fix.

**What I fixed: only the command.** Added `--no-mmap` (drops the duplicate mapping; ~4.5 G fits 6 G). Same binary, same model - finished in 15 minutes with correct text.

## The earlier real failure (F0), for contrast

That one was a code bug I fixed in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp` (commit `17b246b44`): the RVV dot-product helpers initialized their accumulator with a `_tu` intrinsic merging into an uninitialized register. GCC re-emitted that init under the wrong vector type, leaving 6 of 8 accumulator registers as garbage, so qwen35's delta-net exploded and the 27B generated nonsense. The fix uses a plain, well-defined init; after it, rv64 output matches the x86 host exactly.
