# Bonsai 8B and 27B on andesim hybrid: one kernel stack, 11.23x and 11.86x

Engine `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (VLEN 1024, ELEN 64, real L3 RTL); 8B measured
2026-08-04, 27B measured 2026-08-05..06. The same Q1_0 optimization chain
(repack -> prefetch -> vd4dots) carries from 4B to 8B to 27B with the
per-element cost almost unchanged:

| model | arch   | K=51 node                       | pristine -> final cycles  | speedup |
|-------|--------|---------------------------------|---------------------------|---------|
| 8B    | qwen3  | blk.7.attn_v [4096 x 1024]      | 7,278,168 -> 648,246      | 11.23x  |
| 27B   | qwen35 | blk.6.attn_gate [5120 x 6144]   | 54,314,202 -> 4,578,346   | 11.86x  |

## Part 1 - what must change to run the 8B model

The 4B recipe carries over unchanged: same four binaries, same engine, same
ROI marker at K=51 - two flags and zero rebuilds. Both flags exist because
the 8B model presses against the 2 GiB guest RAM window.

- **`--mem-size 2097148K`** (andesim flag). The exact hybrid maximum:
  2 GiB minus the 4 KiB hybrid scratch area. Hybrid mode rejects `2G`
  outright, so this literal value is required.
- **`--no-mmap`** (llama.cpp flag). On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack buffer type
  accepts these tensors, so with mmap the 1,099 MiB file mapping AND the
  931 MiB repack buffer are both resident at load time. `--no-mmap` drops
  the mapping; everything else fits with 565 MiB to spare.

Guest RAM demand at load, drawn to scale (1 char = 64 MiB):

```
              0    512  1024 1536 2048 = the 2 GiB window
              |----|----|----|----|
default (mmap) MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMRRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO   2,582 MiB: FAILS, 534 over
with --no-mmap RRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO                    1,483 MiB: fits, 565 free
              |----|----|----|----|
M = file mapping 1,099   R = repack buffer 931
O = other 552 (non-repacked weights 168 + KV cache 72 at -c 512 + compute 312)
```

```bash
cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

## Part 2 - what must change to run the 27B model

The 27B (3.8 GB, qwen35) needs three lifts beyond the 8B recipe. Binaries
and engine stay the same.

1. **Guest RAM beyond 2 GiB.** The andesim runtime now places guest RAM at
   the high window 0x8_00000000 (DRAM alias + DRAM_EXT, contiguous) whenever
   `--mem-size` exceeds the low window, in both fast and hybrid modes, up to
   16G. The vsim leg maps a low-2G alias over the same memory so the RTL
   still fetches the low-linked code. At or below 2 GiB the historical map
   is kept, so every recorded cycle number stays comparable (re-measured
   bit-identical). Commits: andesim `5c134e5`/`1edb88d`/`9d10a6d`,
   vsim_andesim `e874381`.
2. **`--mem-size 6G --no-mmap`.** With mmap, the 3,891 MiB mapping plus the
   ~3.1 GiB repack buffer exceed 6G. `--no-mmap` fits with room to spare.
   (An over-budget mmap load does NOT fail fast at this size - it grinds -
   so the flag is mandatory at 6G.)
3. **The rv64 vec_dot fix** (llama.cpp `17b246b44`). qwen35's delta-net
   exercises `ggml_vec_dot_f32`, whose RVV accumulator init used a `_tu`
   merge into an uninitialized register; GCC 14 could re-materialize it
   under the wrong vector type, corrupting 6 of 8 accumulator registers.
   Fixed with a plain init at vlmax. qwen3 (4B/8B) never calls this helper
   on its decode path, so their results were always correct and unchanged.
   After the fix, 27B rv64 output matches the x86 host byte-for-byte at
   temp 0 ("The capital of France is Paris.").

```bash
cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 6G --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

On qwen35's graph, compiled-in K=51 lands on the layer-6 attention gate
(`blk.6.attn_gate.weight [5120 x 6144]`, nrows=2) - self-reported by the
`[roi]` line, so the node identity is checked, not assumed.

## Part 3 - speedups

RTL cycles per model, drawn to scale. The two charts use different scales
(8B: 1 char = 150k cycles; 27B: 1 char = 1.1M, about the 7.5x node-size
ratio) - the bars look alike because the speedups are alike.

```
8B, K=51 = attn_v [4096 x 1024]                    (1 char = 150k cycles)
pristine   ################################################# 7,278,168   1.00x
repack     #######################                           3,475,147   2.09x
+prefetch  ###############                                   2,218,540   3.28x
+vd4dots   ####                                                648,246  11.23x

27B, K=51 = attn_gate [5120 x 6144]                (1 char = 1.1M cycles)
pristine   ################################################# 54,314,202  1.00x
repack     #######################                           25,629,722  2.12x
+prefetch  ###############                                   16,317,304  3.33x
+vd4dots   ####                                               4,578,346 11.86x
```

| build          | 8B cycles | 8B total | 27B cycles | 27B total |
|----------------|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| pristine       | 7,278,168 | 1.00x    | 54,314,202 | 1.00x     |
| repack         | 3,475,147 | 2.09x    | 25,629,722 | 2.12x     |
| + prefetch     | 2,218,540 | 3.28x    | 16,317,304 | 3.33x     |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 648,246   | **11.23x** | 4,578,346 | **11.86x** |

The chain transfers because the per-element cost barely moves across an
8.6x range of node sizes. Repack and prefetch are essentially
shape-invariant; vd4dots varies a few percent with the streamed bytes per
row:

| build          | 4B cyc/elem | 8B cyc/elem | 27B cyc/elem |
|----------------|-------------|-------------|--------------|
| pristine       | 1.707       | 1.735       | 1.727        |
| repack         | 0.818       | 0.829       | 0.815        |
| + prefetch     | 0.528       | 0.529       | 0.519        |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 0.138       | 0.155       | 0.146        |

Elements per node: 4B 2560x1024, 8B 4096x1024, 27B 5120x6144; nrows=2 in
all three, so per-activation numbers are these values halved.

<details>
<summary>Appendix - run environment and verification</summary>

- **Models**: Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf 1.16 GB (qwen3, 36 layers, n_embd 4096);
  Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf 3.8 GB (qwen35 hybrid attention, n_embd 5120).
- **Builds**: `bin-pristine` (REPACK=OFF), `bin-baseline` (REPACK=ON, PF=0),
  `bin-prefetch` (PF=1), `bin-d4` (PF=1, Q1_D4=1, includes F9). The vec_dot
  fix is measurement-neutral: fixed-binary 4B K=51 = 362,797 vs 362,799
  recorded (2 cycles, link-layout noise).
- **Success check**: read the output, not the exit code - a good run prints
  the `[roi]` node self-check followed by `[andesim] <N> cycles`.
- **Correctness**: 27B fast-mode run at 6G prints "The capital of France is
  Paris." (temp 0), matching the x86 host reference.
- **Reproducibility**: vsim is deterministic; node counts are repeat-stable.
  Cross-window (>2G vs legacy) comparisons carry a ~0.3% layout-noise bound;
  same-window numbers are exact.
- **Logs**: `~/tmp/8b-runs/{8b,27b}-hybrid-*-k51.log`

</details>

# Running Bonsai-8B on andesim hybrid: 2 flags, 0 rebuilds, 11.23x

2026-08-04, engine `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (VLEN 1024, ELEN 64, real L3 RTL).
The 4B flow extends to the 8B model with two flags and no rebuild, and the
Q1_0 optimization chain gives **7,278,168 -> 648,246 cycles = 11.23x** on the
K=51 node (layer 7 V projection, `blk.7.attn_v.weight [4096 x 1024]`, nrows=2).

## Part 1 - what must change to run the 8B model

The 4B recipe carries over unchanged: same four binaries, same engine, same
ROI marker at K=51. The model file is a runtime argument. Only two flags are
new, and both exist because the 8B model presses against the 2 GiB guest RAM
window.

- **`--mem-size 2097148K`** (andesim flag). The exact hybrid maximum:
  2 GiB minus the 4 KiB hybrid scratch area. Hybrid mode rejects `2G`
  outright (only fast mode accepts it), so this literal value is required.
- **`--no-mmap`** (llama.cpp flag). On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack buffer type
  accepts these tensors, so with mmap the 1,099 MiB file mapping AND the
  931 MiB repack buffer are both resident at load time. Together with the
  other buffers that exceeds the window. `--no-mmap` drops the mapping;
  everything else fits with 565 MiB to spare.

Guest RAM demand at load, drawn to scale (1 char = 64 MiB):

```
              0    512  1024 1536 2048 = the 2 GiB window
              |----|----|----|----|
default (mmap) MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMRRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO   2,582 MiB: FAILS, 534 over
with --no-mmap RRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO                    1,483 MiB: fits, 565 free
              |----|----|----|----|
M = file mapping 1,099   R = repack buffer 931
O = other 552 (non-repacked weights 168 + KV cache 72 at -c 512 + compute 312)
```

Removing the file mapping is the whole fix: the repacked copy is the one the
kernels read, so the mapping was pure duplication.

The full command (the two 8B flags are the only changes vs 4B):

```bash
cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

<details>
<summary>Why the binaries need no rebuild</summary>

The ROI marker counts MUL_MAT nodes, not shapes. Bonsai-8B is the same qwen3
architecture as 4B (36 layers, 253 MUL_MAT per token), so compiled-in K=51
lands on the same node: the layer-7 V projection. Only its shape grows,
2560x1024 -> 4096x1024. Each run self-reports the node, so this is checked,
not assumed:

```
[roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [4096 x 1024] nrows=2
```

The repack gate also passes untouched: 1024 output rows, 1024 mod 64 = 0.

</details>

## Part 2 - speedup on the 8B node

Same optimization chain as 4B, measured on the K=51 node (RTL cycles).
Every stage keeps output bit-exact.

RTL cycles, drawn to scale (1 char = 150k cycles):

```
pristine   #################################################  7,278,168   1.00x
repack     #######################                            3,475,147   2.09x
+prefetch  ###############                                    2,218,540   3.28x
+vd4dots   ####                                                 648,246  11.23x
```

| build          | cycles    | step  | total speedup | 4B total (ref) |
|----------------|-----------|-------|---------------|----------------|
| pristine       | 7,278,168 | -     | 1.00x         | 1.00x          |
| repack         | 3,475,147 | 2.09x | 2.09x         | 2.09x          |
| + prefetch     | 2,218,540 | 1.57x | 3.28x         | 3.23x          |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 648,246   | 3.42x | **11.23x**    | 12.34x         |

The chain transfers to 8B almost exactly. Repack and prefetch cost the same
cycles per element as on 4B - the prefetch stage lands at 0.264 cyc/elem/act,
inside the 0.261-0.265 band measured across all five 4B shapes - so their 8B
cycle counts are simply 1.6x the 4B counts, which is the element ratio
(4096/2560). The vd4dots stage is the one place the models differ: 0.155 vs
0.138 cyc/elem (+12%), which accounts for the whole 11.23x-vs-12.34x gap.

<details>
<summary>Per-element comparison, 8B vs 4B</summary>

| build          | 8B cyc/elem | 4B cyc/elem | delta  |
|----------------|-------------|-------------|--------|
| pristine       | 1.735       | 1.707       | +1.6%  |
| repack         | 0.829       | 0.818       | +1.3%  |
| + prefetch     | 0.529       | 0.528       | +0.2%  |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 0.155       | 0.138       | +11.7% |

Elements per node: 8B 4096x1024, 4B 2560x1024; nrows=2 in both, so
per-activation numbers are these values halved.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Appendix - run environment and verification</summary>

- **Model**: `Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf`, 1.16 GB - qwen3, 36 layers, n_embd 4096,
  n_head_kv 8.
- **Builds**: `bin-pristine` (REPACK=OFF), `bin-baseline` (REPACK=ON, PF=0),
  `bin-prefetch` (PF=1), `bin-d4` (PF=1, Q1_D4=1, includes the F9 vsetvli
  batching).
- **Success check**: read the output, not the exit code - a good run prints
  the `[roi]` node self-check followed by `[andesim] <N> cycles`.
- **Reproducibility**: vsim is deterministic; these node counts are
  repeat-stable.
- **Throughput tip**: runs are independent (per-run temp dirs and shm files),
  so the four measurements ran in parallel; the slowest (pristine, ~7.3M RTL
  cycles) sets the wall time.
- **Logs**: `~/tmp/8b-runs/8b-hybrid-{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k51.log`

</details>

The vd4dots stage is the one place the models differ: 0.155 vs 0.138 cyc/elem (+12%), which accounts for the whole 11.23x-vs-12.34x gap.

### U10h. vlinux mmap-backed load grinds at multi-GB scale [PLANNED]

- Description: mmap-based model loading is pathologically slow at 27B scale
  even when memory FITS. Measured 2026-08-06, fast mode, bin-d4-fixed:
  27B at 6G with mmap (over budget: 3,891 MiB mapping + ~3.1 GiB repack)
  ground >31 h with no output and no fail-fast; 27B at 8G with mmap (FITS,
  ~7.3 GiB demand) was still inside "load the model" after 4 h at 99% CPU;
  the identical run with --no-mmap completed everything in ~15 min. The 8B
  1,099 MiB mapping loads fine (~25 min total at 3G), so the cost is
  super-linear in mapping size - suspect O(pages^2) behavior in the vlinux
  mm/page-fault path (~950k pages at 27B vs ~270k at 8B), not TCG itself.
- Consequence today: --no-mmap is MANDATORY for multi-GB models regardless
  of --mem-size; U10's "resident with NO --no-mmap" target is functionally
  met only for models whose mapping is ~1 GiB or smaller.
- Diagnosis plan when resumed: instrument runtime/linux/mm.c fault path
  (count faults + cycles per fault at 8B vs 27B); if the per-fault cost
  grows with mapping size, replace the linear VMA/page lookup with an
  interval structure or pre-fault whole mappings on mmap().
- Key files: runtime/linux/mm.c, mm.h, syscall plumbing for mmap/read.
- Depends on: nothing (independent QoL fix; measurement flow unaffected).
- State: PLANNED

content.text:
The watchdog surfaced a new, separate issue - broken down here for your decision, not yet fixed:

**Finding: vlinux's mmap-backed loading grinds at multi-GB scale even when memory fits.** The 8G run had ~700 MiB of headroom, yet after 4 hours it was still inside "load the model" at 99% CPU - while the identical run with `--no-mmap` finished everything in 15 minutes. So my earlier explanation was incomplete: the 31-hour run was over budget AND on this slow path; the slow path exists independently.

The scaling pattern points at the mechanism: the 8B's 1.1 GB mapping loads fine (~25 min total), the 27B's 3.8 GB collapses - super-linear in mapping size, consistent with something like O(pages²) in the vlinux memory-management fault path (~950k pages at 27B vs ~270k at 8B), rather than TCG slowness.

What I did:

1. Killed the 8G run (4 h of evidence was enough; nothing waits on it).
2. Recorded it as **U10h (PLANNED)** in the andesim roadmap with the measurements and a diagnosis plan (instrument `runtime/linux/mm.c` fault counts/costs at 8B vs 27B; likely fix is an interval-based page lookup or pre-faulting whole mappings). Committed as `f753b93`.
3. Marked **U10g fully DONE** in the same commit, with the honest deviation note: the "no `--no-mmap` needed" convenience target is only met for ~1 GB-and-smaller mappings today.
4. Updated my memory notes: `--no-mmap` is mandatory for multi-GB models at any `--mem-size` until U10h is fixed.

Nothing blocks on this - the measurement flow and all results are unaffected. Say the word if you want me to take on U10h now, or it stays parked as documented.

message.content: what is U10h?

content.text:
U10h is the name I gave the newly found bug in the andesim roadmap - the next item in the "U10x" series that tracks the Linux-runtime / guest-RAM work (U10a...U10g were the >2 GiB lift you already have).

**What it says:** loading a model through `mmap` under vlinux (andesim's proxy kernel) becomes absurdly slow when the mapped file is large - even when memory is enough.

**The evidence behind it:**

| run (27B, fast mode, same binary) | result |
|---|---|
| 6G, `--no-mmap` | everything done in ~15 min, correct text |
| 8G, mmap (fits: needs ~7.3 G) | still stuck in "load" after 4 h at 99% CPU |
| 6G, mmap (over budget) | ground 31+ h, no output, no fail-fast |
| 8B 1.1 GB mapping (for contrast) | loads fine, ~25 min total |

So the cost is super-linear in mapping size: 3.5x more file = far more than 3.5x slower. My suspicion is the vlinux memory-management fault path handles each page fault by walking a linear structure, giving roughly O(pages²) total work - the 27B maps ~950k pages vs the 8B's ~270k, which would make it ~12x more expensive per fault on top of 3.5x more faults.

**Planned fix (not started):** instrument `runtime/linux/mm.c` to count faults and cost per fault at 8B vs 27B; if the per-fault cost grows with mapping size, replace the linear lookup with an interval structure, or simply pre-fault the whole mapping at `mmap()` time.

**Impact today:** none on your results - it only means `--no-mmap` stays mandatory for multi-GB models, which is already how all measurements were run. It's parked as PLANNED in `andesim/ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` (commit `f753b93`) until you decide it's worth fixing.
